To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the redirection schemes in content networks can be improved by treating Web pages as a single entity, rather than as individual components.
the performance of a Web page is not affected by the number of servers used to serve the page, but by how many servers are used to serve the same page to a single client.

1) the performance of redirection schemes that use a single redirection server for all parts of a page is better than the performance of redirection that use a redirection server for each part of the page; 2) the performance of the redirection scheme that uses a single redirection server is better than the redirection scheme that does not use a redirection server; and 3) the performance of a redirection scheme that uses two redirection servers is better than a redirection scheme that does use a redirection server.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the impact of redirection schemes on the performance of Web page viewing?
understanding the performance implications of the different redirection schemes that are used in modern CDNs.
the performance of content distribution networks and how the performance can be improved by the use of different redirection schemes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
redirection schemes that use only one server per Web page are superior to schemes that use multiple servers for a single page.
the redirection schemes that we have studied do not yield optimal performance, and that a more intelligent redirection scheme is needed.
the performance of the redirection schemes depends heavily on the network environment and the Web page characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we should not replicate parts of Web pages, we rather should replicate the whole page, and that we should not use redirection schemes that require the clients to access more than one server to retrieve a Web page.
the current redirection schemes in content networks are sub-optimal, and we should consider using a single redirection server for each page.
the redirection schemes used in current content distribution systems are not optimal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when replicating content, we should be careful about the way the content is split and the redirection schemes used to direct clients to different copies.
when designing content distribution networks, we should consider not only the performance of a single request, but also how the different requests in a Web page are handled.
we should be very careful in designing content distribution systems and that the performance of the system is not necessarily a function of the number of servers alone.
